title: CKA vs CKAD: Which Kubernetes Cert Fits Your Role?
subtitle: Which Kubernetes cert to choose based on the job you actually do

pros: The reference Kubernetes cert for ops / SRE / Platform Engineer roles.
Senior median salary of €72k in France, €70k in Belgium, €88k in Luxembourg (Hays 2026).
Hands-on format (live lab) — no multiple-choice cramming, you do real k8s work.
Covers the whole cluster: control plane, etcd, networking, troubleshooting, security.
cons: Very technical — you need to be able to debug a broken cluster in 30 minutes.
$395 for the exam, ~80-120 hours of realistic prep if you haven't run a cluster.
Heavy time pressure (2 hours for ~15-20 tasks in the terminal).
certs.bestFor: You're targeting Platform Engineer, SRE, or DevOps with cluster responsibility. You'll be the one debugging at 3 a.m.

pros: More approachable than the CKA — focused on Pods / Deployments / Services / ConfigMaps, not the control plane.
Perfect for backend developers who deploy their code on K8s.
The same hands-on format as the CKA, but with developer tasks (create a Pod with an init container, expose a Service, etc.).
A strong résumé signal for cloud-native developer roles (backend, microservices).
cons: Less recognized than the CKA in pure ops/infra — a Platform Engineer role wants the CKA, not the CKAD.
Same price as the CKA ($395) for a cert perceived as 'easier'.
Only covers the application layer: if you want to manage a cluster, it's the wrong cert.
certs.bestFor: You're a developer (Go, Java, Python, Node) who deploys to K8s regularly. You want to master the developer side without becoming a cluster admin.

verdicts.profile: You're a Platform Engineer, SRE, or DevOps engineer responsible for a production cluster.
verdicts.why: The CKA covers the control plane, etcd, cluster troubleshooting, networking and security. It's your cert. The CKAD doesn't qualify you for these roles.

verdicts.profile: You're a backend developer deploying your services on Kubernetes.
verdicts.why: The CKAD tests exactly your daily work: creating Deployments, configuring ConfigMaps/Secrets, exposing Services, managing liveness/readiness probes. The CKA would be overkill.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a Cloud Architect / Platform Lead role.
verdicts.why: At lead level, you're expected to manage a cluster end to end. The CKA is expected; the CKAD alone is seen as insufficient.

verdicts.profile: You're new to Kubernetes and torn between the two.
verdicts.why: Start with the CKAD: a gentler learning curve, focused on the concepts you'll use every day as a developer. The CKA will come naturally afterward if you drift toward ops.

verdicts.profile: You're aiming for the CKA + CKAD + CKS (Security) trifecta.
verdicts.why: If you're taking all 3, do the CKA first: it gives you the cluster foundations the CKS assumes. The CKAD can follow as a complement within 2-3 months.

tldr: CKA = you run the cluster. CKAD = you deploy onto it. Both cost $395, both are hands-on labs — the right choice is the one that matches your actual job, not the 'more recognized' one (the CKA is more recognized, but pointless if you're a backend developer).
